name: Campsis

project_scope.note: One canonical species in this genus in the current learner; comparisons to other genera are NOT separate canonical species.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Opposite OD D-pinnately compound leaves with ~7–11 coarsely serrate leaflets; woody vine attaching to bark/walls using adventitious aerial ROOTLETS, not a terminal tendril. Terminal clusters of orange/red tubular trumpet blooms. Long two-valved capsules with flat winged seeds.
shared_genus_recognition.emphasis: USE LEAF STRUCTURE / CLIMBING MECHANISM first; flower color alone is poor Bignoniaceae ID. Confirm with long 2-valved capsule and seeds.
shared_genus_recognition.family_note: Bignoniaceae generally has bilateral trumpet-shaped flowers with four fertile didynamous stamens + reduced fifth, and capsules with winged or haired seeds.

genus_comparison_matrix.Campsis: Many small adventitious aerial rootlets along stems attaching directly to support

genus_comparison_matrix.Bignonia: Opposite leaves mostly 2 leaflets + central branched tendril
genus_comparison_matrix.Chilopsis: Simple, narrow strap/linear leaves; alternate/opposite variable

genus_comparison_matrix.Bignonia: Usually whole/entire margins on two large leaflets
genus_comparison_matrix.Chilopsis: Entire margins on narrow simple blade

genus_comparison_matrix.Campsis: Orange to reddish-orange large trumpet-shaped terminal clusters
genus_comparison_matrix.Bignonia: Orange-red trumpets often with yellow-lined throat
genus_comparison_matrix.Chilopsis: Pink, white or lavender ruffled-trumpet flowers

genus_comparison_matrix.Campsis: Long narrow thick-walled 2-valved capsules with many papery winged seeds
genus_comparison_matrix.Bignonia: Long flattened 2-valved capsules with many winged seeds
genus_comparison_matrix.Chilopsis: Very narrow long capsules, with hairy/winglike-fringed seeds

genus_comparison_matrix.Campsis: Climber often dense on trees, fences and walls; roots also produce shoots
genus_comparison_matrix.Bignonia: Climber often evergreen/semi-evergreen in woodland edges
genus_comparison_matrix.Chilopsis: Dry-wash West Texas type tree; can be planted outside range

look_here_first_sequence: Check whether the plant is climbing; inspect attachment point instead of flower color.
Look at a complete leaf: odd-pinnate 7–11 serrated leaflets = Campsis versus 2 leaflets + tendril = Bignonia.
Find short adhesive aerial roots arising from the STEM, not from leaf-tip tendril.
Check trumpet flowers and two-valved winged-seed capsule as reproductive confirmation.
lookalikes_and_scientific_cautions: Lonicera sempervirens (coral honeysuckle) has simple opposite leaves and berries, not long winged-seed capsules.
Dolichandra unguis-cati/catclaw vine has claw-tipped tendrils; look for tendril origin.
Campsis grandiflora in cultivation can be confused; verify leaf and attachment characters, not bloom color.
Campsis radicans has a canonical project confirmed-native label; do not extend that status to other family members.

Campsis odd-pinnate serrate and Bignonia two-leaflet + terminal adhesive tendril same frame scale
2 longitudinal valves and flat paper-winged seeds; compare honey-suckle berries
four fertile stamens, staminode, bilateral corolla, corolla throat
flowering climber attached to tree by aerial roots
